titleEn: Real Estate Agent English Conversation — 40 Units
subtitleZh: 看對話 → 聽發音 → 跟讀／角色扮演 → 抽換名詞舉一反三
subtitleEn: Dialogues, pronunciation, role-play, and swappable slots for practice.
disclaimerZh: 對話僅供溝通練習；正式交易請依現行加州法規、合約與公司政策。

units.scenario: 週年會／社區活動／首次見面，建立信任。
units.cramRef: 專業形象；Agency 起點（Customer → 之後才可能變 Client）。

phrases.en: Hi, I'm {{agent_name}} with {{brokerage}}.
phrases.zh: 你好，我是某某經紀人，任職於…

phrases.en: I help buyers and sellers in {{city}}.
May I ask what brings you here today?
phrases.zh: 方便問今天什麼事找上門？

dialogue.en: Hi, I'm {{agent_name}} with {{brokerage}}. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. We're thinking about buying in {{city}}.
Great. I help buyers and sellers in {{city}}. May I ask what brings you here today?
We're just starting to look.
Perfect. No pressure—happy to answer questions and share what the market looks like.

drills: 用自己的名字換成 `{{agent_name}}` 說三遍開場。
對方說 “We're just browsing.” 回一句不施壓的歡迎。
把 `{{city}}` 換成三個不同城市；把 “buying” 改成 “selling” 再說一次。

units.scenario: 買家來電問某房源；約看屋時間。
units.cramRef: Showing；Ready, willing and able（之後才談）。

phrases.en: Thanks for calling about {{address}}.
Are you available {{time}}?
I'll text you the gate code and parking tips.
phrases.zh: 我會簡訊門禁碼與停車提醒

dialogue.en: Thanks for calling about the {{property_type}} at {{address}}. This is {{agent_name}}.
Hi. Can we see it this weekend?
Absolutely. Are you available {{time}}?
That works.
Great. I'll confirm and text you the address, gate code, and parking tips.

drills: 對方說 “We're free after 2.” → 你提出兩個時段選項。
換三組 `{{address}}` + `{{time}}`；練習「確認＋簡訊預告」收尾。

units.scenario: 第一次諮詢，釐清預算、區域、房型（不引導歧視條件）。
units.cramRef: Demand／Utility；Situs（地利）；Budget。
units.fairHousingNote: 不要問／不要假設種族、宗教、家庭組成「該住哪」；只談客戶**主動提出**的區域與生活需求。

phrases.en: What are your must-haves versus nice-to-haves?
phrases.zh: 必要條件 vs 加分項？

phrases.en: What's a comfortable monthly payment range?
Which areas are on your short list?

dialogue.en: To save you time, what are your must-haves versus nice-to-haves?
We need {{beds}} bedrooms and a {{must_have}}.
Got it. What's a comfortable price range—or monthly payment range—for you?
Around {{budget}}.
And which areas are on your short list in {{city}}?
Mostly {{neighborhood}}.
Perfect. I'll pull options that match those priorities.

drills: 換 `{{beds}}`、`{{must_have}}`、`{{budget}}` 各兩組，重講一次。

units.scenario: 抵達屋外，開場、戴鞋套、尊重屋主財物。
units.cramRef: Showing 專業度；Fiduciary／注意義務（對委託人）。

phrases.en: Please feel free to take your time.
Let me know if you'd like me to open any cabinets.
We'll leave everything as we found it.

dialogue.en: Welcome! This is {{address}}. Before we go in—any questions from the photos?
Not yet. We're excited.
Great. Please feel free to take your time. Let me know if you'd like me to open any cabinets or the garage.
Can we see the backyard first?
Of course—right this way.

drills: 練習：進門前說一句安全／禮儀提醒（鞋套、寵物、請勿飲食）。

units.scenario: 邊走邊介紹格局與亮點。
units.cramRef: Real property／features；Utility。

phrases.en: This home is about {{sqft}} square feet.
The standout feature is the {{feature}}.
Built in {{year_built}}, with updates in the kitchen.

dialogue.en: As we walk in, notice the {{feature}}. The home is about {{sqft}} square feet with {{beds}} beds and {{baths}} baths.
Is the flooring new?
The listing notes updated flooring in the main living area. We can confirm details in the disclosures.

drills: 用同一句型輪換 4 個 `{{feature}}`（kitchen／yard／garage／view）。

units.titleEn: Location & Neighborhood — Fair Housing Safe Talk
units.scenario: 談交通、便利、生活機能；**不**談「適合哪種人」。
units.cramRef: Situs；⚠ Steering／Implicit bias。

phrases.en: This area is popular for its parks and commute options.
I can share school rating websites and public data—you can decide what matters to you.
What lifestyle features matter most to you—walkability, quiet streets, or shopping?

dialogue.en: How's the neighborhood?
Location-wise, {{neighborhood}} is known for {{feature}}. What matters most for you day to day?
A quieter street and easier commute.
Then let's focus on homes that match those priorities. I can also point you to public data sources for schools and crime maps if you want to research.

drills: 把任何「某種人適合」的句子改成「功能／數據／客戶自選」。

rewrites.unsafe: This is a good area for families like yours.
rewrites.safe: Many buyers like the parks and weekend farmers market.

rewrites.unsafe: You might prefer that side of town.
rewrites.safe: Which side of town fits your commute better?

units.cramRef: Appurtenance（附隨設施概念）；Amenities。

phrases.en: There's a {{garage_spaces}}-car garage. `[1, 2, 3]`
Street parking is {{parking_note}}
HOA amenities include {{amenity}}

dialogue.en: Is parking easy?
There's a {{garage_spaces}}-car garage, and street parking is {{parking_note}}. If this is an HOA community, amenities may include a {{amenity}}—we can verify in the HOA docs.

units.cramRef: Market value ≠ Market price；Listing price。

phrases.en: The list price is {{list_price}}—that's the asking price.
The final sale price is what the parties actually agree on.

dialogue.en: Is {{list_price}} a fair price?
The list price is the seller's asking price. Market value is an opinion of what a ready, willing, and able buyer would likely pay. We can review recent comps and your goals, then decide a strategy.

drills: 用三個不同 `{{list_price}}` 解釋 list／value／sale price 差異（各 20 秒）。

units.cramRef: CMA（非正式）；Sales comparison；調 Comp 不調 Subject。

phrases.en: This is a Comparative Market Analysis—not a formal appraisal.
I looked at similar homes nearby that sold in the last 6–12 months.
Based on the comps, a competitive range looks like {{price_range}}

dialogue.en: Thanks for having me. I'll walk you through a CMA—this is not a formal appraisal.
Okay.
These comps are similar {{property_type}}s in {{neighborhood}}, sold recently. Adjusting for differences, a competitive list range is about {{price_range}}.
Why not list higher?
We can, but overpricing can mean fewer showings. A strategic price often brings stronger interest.

units.cramRef: Listing agreement；Customer→Client。

phrases.en: Today is about your goals, timeline, and how I work.
If we move forward, we'll review the listing paperwork carefully.
What's most important—top dollar, speed, or convenience?

dialogue.en: Thanks for inviting me to {{address}}. Before numbers, what matters most—top dollar, a faster sale, or less hassle?
Mostly top dollar, but we need to move within three months.
Got it. I'll show you a pricing and marketing plan that balances both.

units.cramRef: 衝刺 #49 — 誰賣出都付佣（含屋主自售）。

phrases.en: With an exclusive right-to-sell listing, I'm your exclusive agent for the term.
If the property sells during the listing period, a commission is typically owed—even if you find the buyer yourself.
In return, I provide full marketing, showings coordination, and negotiation support.

dialogue.en: What if my cousin wants to buy?

Under an exclusive right-to-sell agreement, a commission is typically still owed if it sells during the listing term—even with a buyer you introduce. That's why this listing type lets me invest fully in marketing. We can review every clause before you sign.

drills: 用「好處／義務」各兩句說明，避免施壓用語。

units.cramRef: #50 Exclusive agency；#51 Open listing；#53 Procuring cause。

phrases.en: Exclusive agency
phrases.zh: One broker; if **you** sell it yourself, you may owe no commission.

phrases.en: Open listing
phrases.zh: Multiple brokers; usually only the procuring-cause broker gets paid.

dialogue.en: Can I still sell it myself?

With exclusive agency, if you sell it yourself, you often owe no commission—but you still work with one brokerage for agent-procured buyers. With an open listing, several brokers may market it, and payment usually depends on who is the procuring cause. I can compare pros and cons for your situation.

rewrites.safe: One broker; if **you** sell it yourself, you may owe no commission.
Multiple brokers; usually only the procuring-cause broker gets paid.

units.cramRef: #57 Dual agency（須同意與揭露）。練習「說明＋取得知情同意」語氣，非法務細節課。

phrases.en: Dual agency means the same brokerage represents both buyer and seller.
It requires disclosure and informed consent.
Some duties change; I'll explain what I can and cannot do for each side.

dialogue.en: Are you also the listing agent?

In some cases our brokerage may represent both sides—that's dual agency. It requires clear disclosure and your informed consent. I'll explain how confidentiality and negotiation work before anyone proceeds.

phrases.en: Welcome! Please sign in—here's a flyer with the key facts.
The home is {{beds}}/{{baths}}, about {{sqft}} sq ft, listed at {{list_price}}.
Are you working with an agent already?

dialogue.en: Welcome! Feel free to look around. Here's a flyer—{{beds}} beds, {{baths}} baths, listed at {{list_price}}.
Thanks. We're just exploring.
No problem. If you have questions about the layout or next steps, I'm happy to help.

phrases.en: How did the home feel compared with the others?
What would you change if you could?
Should I schedule a second visit {{time}}?

dialogue.en: Thanks again for touring {{address}}. How did it feel compared with the others?
We liked the kitchen, but the backyard felt small.
Helpful. I can send two options with larger yards in a similar budget. Want a second look at this one {{time}}, or focus on new options?

units.cramRef: Offer；Bilateral contract 概念（雙方承諾）。

phrases.en: Based on the comps and your goals, we could offer {{offer_price}}.
We'll include earnest money, timelines, and contingencies.
Once accepted and delivered, we move toward escrow.

dialogue.en: For {{address}}, a competitive offer might be {{offer_price}} with {{loan_type}} financing.
Can we go a little lower?
We can. Let's also decide earnest money and which contingencies you want—so the offer is complete and clear.

units.cramRef: #72 Counteroffer＝拒絕原要約＋新要約；原要約死亡。

phrases.en: A counteroffer rejects the previous offer and creates a new one.
The other side's original offer is no longer on the table.
We can accept, counter again, or walk away.

dialogue.en: The seller countered at {{list_price}} and asked to shorten the inspection period.
So our first offer is gone?
Right—a counter replaces the prior offer. We can accept this counter, send a new counter, or pause. What matters most—price or timeline?

units.cramRef: #74 Earnest money＝誠意金；非契約成立唯一要件。

phrases.en: Earnest money shows good faith; it's usually held in escrow.
It's not the same thing as your down payment, though it may be credited later.
What happens to it if a deal cancels depends on the contract and contingencies.

dialogue.en: How much earnest money do we need?
It varies by market and strategy. Earnest money shows good faith and is typically deposited into escrow. We'll review how it's handled if a contingency allows you to cancel.

units.cramRef: #85–88 Inspection／Appraisal／Finance；條件成就前的退出保護。

phrases.en: inspection contingency
phrases.zh: 檢查後可依合約談判或退出

phrases.en: appraisal contingency
loan / financing contingency

dialogue.en: Contingencies are conditions that protect you for a period of time.
Do we need all of them?
In a hot market, some buyers shorten or waive items—but that increases risk. I'll explain trade-offs; you decide your comfort level.
I recommend a {{inspector}} for {{time}}. After the report, we'll review any {{issue}} items and decide: request repairs, credit, or proceed.
What if it's serious?
Then we use the inspection contingency timeline in your contract and respond in writing.

drills: 輪換 `{{issue}}`：roof／HVAC／plumbing／electrical，練習回報語氣（中性、不恐嚇）。

units.titleZh: 屋況瑕疵討論（安全說法）
units.cramRef: Material fact；Latent vs Patent；不得協助隱瞞。
units.fairHousingNote: 賣方若要求隱瞞重大瑕疵：拒絕配合，並依公司／法規處理（對應衝刺揭露倫理）。

phrases.en: Sellers must disclose known material facts; agents shouldn't hide them.
I'll point you to the disclosure package—please read it carefully.
For technical opinions, rely on qualified inspectors and specialists.

dialogue.en: There's a stain on the ceiling. Is that a big problem?
It's worth investigating. Let's note it for the inspector and review what the seller disclosed. I won't guess about hidden conditions—specialists should evaluate.

units.cramRef: #90 As-is＝未必免揭露；加州仍常須 TDS／已知重大瑕疵。

phrases.en: “As-is” often means the seller prefers not to make repairs.
It does not mean “no disclosures.”
You still review disclosures and may negotiate within your contingency rights.

dialogue.en: We're selling as-is.
Understood—you prefer not to complete repairs. We'll still complete required disclosures for known material facts, and buyers will review those documents.

units.cramRef: #95 Lead-based paint；Pre-1978。

phrases.en: Homes built before 1978 may have lead-based paint.
Federal disclosure rules apply; buyers get the required pamphlets/forms.
If you have concerns, consider a qualified lead assessment.

dialogue.en: This home was built in {{year_built}}. For pre-1978 homes, lead-based paint disclosures are required. You'll receive the standard information so you can review it.

units.cramRef: Appraisal contingency；Appraisal ≠ CMA。

phrases.en: An appraisal is a licensed appraiser's opinion for the lender.
My CMA was a marketing tool—not the same as an appraisal.

dialogue.en: The appraisal came in below the contract price.
What now?
Options often include renegotiating price, covering the gap if you choose and can, or using your appraisal contingency if it still applies. Let's review numbers and your risk tolerance.

units.cramRef: Finance contingency；Loan types。

dialogue.en: Quick update—have you sent the lender everything they asked for?
Almost. They're waiting on one document.
Please send it today if you can. Under your loan contingency timeline, staying on schedule protects your position. Want me to loop in the loan officer for a status check?

drills: `{{loan_type}}`＝conventional／FHA／VA／cash（cash：改說 “no lender timeline, but escrow still has deadlines”）。

units.cramRef: Escrow；Closing；Executory → Executed。

phrases.en: After acceptance, we open escrow and work the checklist to closing.
Closing is when ownership transfers and the deal is completed.
I'll share key dates: deposit, contingencies removal, final walk-through, signing.

dialogue.en: Congratulations—we're in escrow. Target closing is {{closing_date}}：[in 30 days, April 15].
What should we do this week?
Complete your earnest money deposit, schedule inspections, and stay responsive to escrow and your lender.

units.cramRef: Title insurance；Cloud on title（概念：可轉讓性問題）。

dialogue.en: Escrow and title will request IDs and signatures. Title insurance helps protect against certain title risks.
Do we need to be there in person?
Often you can sign electronically if all parties agree—I'll confirm what this escrow requires.

units.cramRef: Deed restriction／CC&Rs；Zoning vs private restriction（口語不深講衝突規則）。

phrases.en: HOA rules can limit how the property is used—pets, rentals, exterior changes.
Please read the CC&Rs and budget before removing contingencies.

dialogue.en: Can I paint the front door any color?
In many HOA communities, exterior changes need approval. Let's check the CC&Rs so you know the rules before you commit.

units.cramRef: Leasehold 類型概念；Lessor／Lessee；Property management。

dialogue.en: Are you looking to rent a {{property_type}} in {{city}}?
Yes—{{beds}} bedrooms, around {{rent}}.
I can share available options and application steps. Typical lease term here is {{lease_term}}, but we'll confirm each listing.

units.cramRef: Security deposit（概念練習；數字以現行法為準，上課勿背死）。

phrases.en: We'll confirm the security deposit amount under current California rules and the lease.
Ask for move-in condition photos and a clear inventory.

dialogue.en: How much is the deposit?
I'll confirm the exact amount for this property and what the lease requires. Also plan for first month's rent and any HOA move-in fees if applicable.

units.cramRef: #129–136 NOI、Cap rate、IRV（口語版）。

phrases.en: Cap rate is basically NOI divided by value.
Higher cap rate often means higher relative risk—or a lower price for the same income.
This is education, not a guarantee of returns.

dialogue.en: What's the cap rate?
Using estimated NOI and the asking price, the indicated cap rate is about {{cap_rate}}：[4.5%, 5%, 6%]. Let's verify income, vacancy, and expenses before you rely on that number.

drills: 練習口算句： “If NOI is about X and price is Y, cap rate is roughly Z.”

units.cramRef: Counter 撤回再回；競爭力 vs 風險。

dialogue.en: There are multiple offers. To be competitive, some buyers strengthen price, earnest money, or timelines.
Should we waive inspections?
Waiving increases risk. Alternatives include shorter inspection periods or pre-inspecting if allowed. I'll outline options; you choose the risk level.

phrases.en: I hear you—price is the biggest decision.
Let's separate wish price from supportable price using comps.
If we list too high, we may miss the first wave of buyers.

dialogue.en: I want {{list_price}}.
I understand. The comps support closer to {{price_range}}. We can list at your number, or we can price to attract urgency. Which outcome matters more—starting high, or maximizing final price?

units.cramRef: Appraisal 須持牌估價師；缺能力須揭露（倫理）。提供「名單」而非保證結果。

dialogue.en: Can you recommend an inspector?
I can share a list of licensed inspectors clients have used. You're free to choose anyone you prefer. I don't guarantee their findings—your contract relies on their professional report.
Congratulations—you're closing today! After recording, you'll receive keys per the agreement.
Anything we should do tonight?
Confirm utilities transfer, keep closing documents safe, and celebrate. If anything looks off at the final walk-through, call me immediately.
Thank you for trusting me with {{address}}. If friends need help buying or selling in {{city}}, I'd be honored to help—or to refer a great colleague.
We will!
I appreciate it. I'll check in after move-in to see if you need vendor recommendations.
Hi {{client_name}}, this is {{agent_name}} with {{brokerage}}.
I'm following up on {{address}}. I have two similar homes that match your {{beds}}-bedroom search.
Please call or text me when you have a moment. Thanks!
Hi {{client_name}} — {{agent_name}} here. Showing confirmed {{time}} at {{address}}.
Parking tip: {{parking_note}}. See you!

units.titleZh: 公平住房安全用語特訓
units.cramRef: #105–109 Implicit bias、Steering、Blockbusting、Redlining。

dialogue.en: You'll feel more comfortable in that area.
Which area matches your commute and budget best?
That neighborhood is changing—sell now.
If your goal is timing the market, we can review recent sales data together.
I know a lender who helps “your community.”
I can share lenders who work with many local buyers; apply with the same process.

rewrites.unsafe: You'll feel more comfortable in that area.
rewrites.safe: Which area matches your commute and budget best?
If your goal is timing the market, we can review recent sales data together.

rewrites.unsafe: I know a lender who helps “your community.”
rewrites.safe: I can share lenders who work with many local buyers; apply with the same process.
